results.content: The optimal MetaHuman mocap workflow for high-end productions integrates full performance capture, combining body, facial, and hand movements using advanced hardware like Xsens suits, Vicon optical systems, or Faceware for facial data, streamed via Live Link in Unreal Engine 5 (UE5) for real-time preview. In UE5’s Sequencer, animations are aligned on the timeline, leveraging MetaHuman’s separate body and face tracks for precise integration, with tools like MetaHuman Animator enhancing facial data syncing.Separate capture records body and face at different times, using playback to match timing. Epic’s MetaHuman Animator enhances facial capture, syncing high-fidelity animations with body mocap using timecode, ensuring lifelike, coordinated performances in professional workflows. * **Use Live Link Face (iOS)**: Use an ARKit-capable iPhone with the Live Link Face app to capture 52 blendshapes and head rotation, streaming to UE5 for real-time MetaHuman facial animation, recorded with Take Recorder.The Live Link Face app on iPhone captures facial data via ARKit, streaming to UE5. ## How do I use Control Rig in UE5 to refine Metahuman mocap animations? To refine MetaHuman mocap animations using UE5’s Control Rig, follow these steps to enhance performance quality:. * **Use Timecode Across Devices**: Feed SMPTE timecode to all devices for automatic alignment in UE5’s Sequencer, supported by MetaHuman Animator and Take Recorder.Timecode ensures frame-accurate alignment across mocap, facial, and audio devices. MetaHuman Animator integrates as an advanced facial capture tool, complementing body mocap and reducing processing time, making it a valuable addition to professional pipelines. * **FBX Workflow**: Export mocap as FBX from software like Rokoko Studio, importing into UE5 with the MetaHuman skeleton or retargeting as needed.FBX supports skeletal and facial animations comprehensively. results.title: 60Hz vs 120Hz Monitors: Which is Better for you? - MAGEX
results.content: For gamers, a 120Hz monitor offers faster and more accurate visuals, enhancing gameplay and providing a competitive edge in high-frame rate games like those on the Xbox Series X. **Video Playback and Professional Work** A 120Hz monitor provides a smoother viewing experience, especially for high-frame-rate videos or fast-moving scenes. While 60Hz monitors are sufficient for most tasks, those prone to eye strain may find the 120Hz refresh rate offers a more comfortable experience. Here’s a breakdown of the differences to help you decide: * A 4K 60Hz display provides 4 times the resolution of 1080p, making it ideal for tasks that benefit from sharper visuals, like graphic design, video editing, or watching high-definition content. * Casual or single-player gamers, or anyone focused on graphical quality, may find 4K 60Hz more appealing due to the visual fidelity it offers, especially on high-end consoles or powerful PCs. In short, 1080p 120Hz is ideal for those who prioritize fast, responsive gameplay, while 4K 60Hz is better suited for users who want stunning visuals and detail for media consumption and slower-paced activities. If you frequently work with or watch high-frame-rate content, such as 4K Ultra HD videos or HDR media, a 120Hz monitor improves motion fluidity. For users not involved in fast-paced gaming or high-speed video work, a 60Hz monitor provides reliable performance at a lower cost. With 120Hz, you’ll experience reduced motion blur and a more fluid display compared to 60Hz. Although professional players might prefer even higher refresh rates (like 144Hz or 240Hz), 120Hz is generally sufficient for most players to stay competitive and enjoy a smooth gaming experience. However, for fast-paced, competitive games, a higher refresh rate like 120Hz or 144Hz can offer smoother gameplay, reduced motion blur, and quicker responsiveness, which can give you an advantage. Is a 120Hz monitor good for FPS games?** A 120Hz monitor is a solid choice for FPS games as it provides a smoother and more responsive experience than 60Hz. While 144Hz and higher can offer slight improvements, 120Hz is generally more than adequate for most players and makes fast-paced games more enjoyable. It’s great for visually rich, single-player games, although competitive gamers might prefer higher refresh rates like 120Hz or 144Hz, even at lower resolutions.
